server.maintainedFrom: the Maintenance and Release Schedule of nextcloud/server

tools.label: ESLint
tools.why: nothing checks the frontend sources, so a wrong import is found by the build or not at all
tools.legacyWhy: ESLint 9 reads the flat config only; the eslintrc form, an .eslintrc file or the eslintConfig key in package.json, is ignored unless the run is pinned to ESLint 8

tools.label: Stylelint
tools.why: stylesheets are unchecked, and a mistake in CSS fails silently instead of loudly

tools.label: Psalm
tools.why: the PHP side has no static analysis, which is what catches a wrong type before the server does

tools.label: PHPUnit
tools.why: there is no test harness in the checkout, so nothing can be run against a change

tools.label: PHP-CS-Fixer
tools.why: no coding standard is applied to the PHP sources, so formatting is settled in review instead of by a command

tools.label: REUSE
tools.why: licensing is not machine-checkable, which the App Store and every distribution ask for

tools.label: EditorConfig
tools.why: indentation is whatever each contributor's editor does

lines: Version drift: appinfo/info.xml says 1.2.6, package.json says 1.0.0.

make version of ncmake bumps info.xml, composer.json and package.json and re-syncs package-lock.json in one step, so they cannot drift apart. ncmake's lint-version workflow fails a push or a pull request on exactly this drift. The App Store and the server read info.xml, npm and composer read their own manifest. Whichever is behind, a release ends up carrying more than one version number, and only one of them reaches the user.
appinfo/info.xml states no <repository>.
<repository> is the only machine-readable link from a published release back to the source it was built from. Without it nothing that reads the release can tell where its source is.
<website> is not set either.
Declares Nextcloud 25 to 27; the oldest maintained major is 33 (the Maintenance and Release Schedule of nextcloud/server), the newest released 35 (the release tags of nextcloud/server).
max-version 27 is below the oldest maintained major (33, the Maintenance and Release Schedule of nextcloud/server), so the release covers only servers that no longer receive fixes.
min-version 25 reaches below the oldest maintained major (33), which means the code has to keep working with APIs that are no longer tested upstream.
package.json without a lockfile.
Every install resolves the ranges afresh, so two builds of the same commit can contain different code, and npm ci - what CI uses - does not run at all.
package.json scripts stylelint, stylelint:fix call stylelint, and no Stylelint configuration is in the checkout.
stylelint src/**/*.{css,scss,vue}
composer.json scripts cs:check, cs:fix call php-cs-fixer, and no PHP-CS-Fixer configuration is in the checkout.
php-cs-fixer fix --dry-run --diff
The command is there to be run, so whoever runs it gets a tool that has nothing to go by - and CI, if it runs the script, reports the failure as the change under test.
.github/workflows/main.yml runs the script test, which package.json does not declare.
The package manager stops at that step, so the job fails on every run, whatever the change under test. Run with --if-present, a script is optional.
appinfo/info.xml caps PHP at max-version 8.4.
A server on a newer PHP refuses to enable the app, so this cap has to be raised deliberately with every PHP release, not left where it was.
Node 14 stated in main.yml.
Not stated in engines.node in package.json, .nvmrc, so nothing keeps the other places from drifting away from it.
Tooling in the checkout: ESLint (.eslintrc.js, superseded form).

ESLint is configured in .eslintrc.js: ESLint 9 reads the flat config only; the eslintrc form, an .eslintrc file or the eslintConfig key in package.json, is ignored unless the run is pinned to ESLint 8.
No Stylelint configuration: stylesheets are unchecked, and a mistake in CSS fails silently instead of loudly.
No Psalm configuration: the PHP side has no static analysis, which is what catches a wrong type before the server does.
No PHPUnit configuration: there is no test harness in the checkout, so nothing can be run against a change.
No PHP-CS-Fixer configuration: no coding standard is applied to the PHP sources, so formatting is settled in review instead of by a command.
No REUSE configuration: licensing is not machine-checkable, which the App Store and every distribution ask for.
No EditorConfig configuration: indentation is whatever each contributor's editor does.
package.json declares the scripts lint, stylelint, which no installed workflow runs.
The template lint-eslint of nextcloud/.github runs lint: make workflows-install W=lint-eslint
The template lint-stylelint of nextcloud/.github runs stylelint: make workflows-install W=lint-stylelint
A check that no workflow runs on a pull request catches only what the contributor who remembers to run it catches.
4 declared packages are named nowhere in the checkout: @nextcloud/auth, @nextcloud/babel-config, @nextcloud/eslint-config, @nextcloud/stylelint-config.

Searched as literal names over 61 files, package.json excluded apart from its non-dependency fields, lockfiles excluded; then as an ESLint shorthand, as what TypeScript takes from a tsconfig, and as a peer of an installed package in package-lock.json. A package loaded some other way is not named anywhere either, so this is a list to check, not a list to remove.
Licence agpl (appinfo/info.xml), AGPL-3.0-or-later (package.json, composer.json).
agpl in appinfo/info.xml is a deprecated App Store value, shown there as AGPLv3+, which is AGPL-3.0-or-later. An SPDX id there needs a <nextcloud> min-version of 31 or higher.
No LICENSES/ directory, so the licence text itself is not in the checkout, which is what REUSE and the distributions check for.
The link of appinfo/info.xml answers.
PHP 7.4 is the floor in appinfo/info.xml and in composer.json, platform 7.4.
The ncmake bootstrap stub is in place (21 lines).
Every directory the shipped PHP reaches through __DIR__ and the frontend through linkTo is in the shipped file set.
